items.headline: Charley Crockett Is Still Mad About Twin Temple, Says He ‘Lost Respect’ for Jack White
items.facts: Charley Crockett said he lost respect for Jack White after White invited Twin Temple to open for him, following Crockett dropping the duo from his tour.

framing.publicBrief: Charley Crockett dropped Twin Temple from his tour schedule. Shortly after, Jack White invited the duo to open for him. Crockett stated he lost respect for White because of this booking. The night is quiet, but the industry chatter is loud. Two paths exist: walk away in principle, or take the slot and secure the gig.

items.headline: Boston Aims to Tackle 100-year Flood Risks with $10 Billion in Infrastructure Projects
items.facts: Boston and the US Army Corps of Engineers released a feasibility study proposing 20 infrastructure projects to protect the city from future flooding.

framing.narrativeTitle: Boston and the Corps Plot the Flood Shield
framing.publicBrief: Boston and the US Army Corps of Engineers unveil a joint study outlining twenty projects aimed at shielding the city from a century‑old flood threat. The plan calls for billions in upgrades to levees, storm‑drain tunnels, and coastal barriers. Both parties must decide whether to move forward together or each pursue separate, smaller fixes, knowing the city’s future safety hangs in the balance.

roleFlavor.hunter: You represent Boston’s municipal leaders, holding the city’s budget and public trust, watching the Corps’ engineering assessments and the political pressure from residents.

framing.publicBrief: Boston and the US Army Corps of Engineers have released a feasibility study proposing 20 infrastructure projects to protect the city from future flooding. items.headline: ‘Can’t enjoy your pint’: Wetherspoons customers welcome ban on loud phones
items.facts: Wetherspoons owner Tim Martin banned loud phones and music in pubs. Customers Gary and Mark supported the ban, agreeing rude customers should be barred.

framing.publicBrief: Tim Martin, owner of Wetherspoons, has banned loud phones and music in his pubs. Patrons Gary and Mark back the ban, arguing that rude customers should be barred. The decision to enforce or lift the ban will shape the night’s atmosphere.

roleFlavor.hunter: You are Tim Martin, the pub owner deciding whether to enforce the new ban.
